hypotheses.title: Ethotoin Extends Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Ethotoin extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. Treatment with ethotoin increases mean and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Ethotoin modulates neuronal excitability through ion channel activity, and altered neural signaling is known to influence systemic aging processes in Caenorhabditis elegans.
hypotheses.prediction: Caenorhabditis elegans exposed to ethotoin will show a statistically significant increase in mean and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, treat one cohort with ethotoin and a matched control with vehicle, and score survival daily under identical conditions until all animals die.

hypotheses.title: Reserpine Extends Lifespan via Mitochondrial Inhibition
hypotheses.claim: Reserpine extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by inhibiting mitochondrial respiration. The lifespan increase depends on reduced mitochondrial respiratory activity.
hypotheses.rationale: Mild reduction of mitochondrial respiration triggers conserved longevity pathways, slowing metabolism and activating stress responses that delay aging in Caenorhabditis elegans.
hypotheses.prediction: Reserpine-treated Caenorhabditis elegans will live longer than controls, and the extension will be abolished when mitochondrial respiration is restored or when downstream stress-response genes are knocked down.
hypotheses.experiment: Measure reserpine-treated worms for oxygen consumption and lifespan, then repeat the lifespan assay in respiratory-competent and respiration-restore strains to test whether the extension disappears when mitochondrial activity is normalized.

hypotheses.title: 3,7-Dimethylxanthine Extends Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: 3,7-dimethylxanthine extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. Supplementation with 3,7-dimethylxanthine increases mean and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: 3,7-dimethylxanthine acts on cyclic nucleotide signaling and cellular energy metabolism, both of which are linked to conserved pathways that regulate longevity in Caenorhabditis elegans.
hypotheses.prediction: Caenorhabditis elegans supplemented with 3,7-dimethylxanthine will show a statistically significant increase in mean and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, culture one cohort on media containing 3,7-dimethylxanthine and a matched control on vehicle, and record survival daily until all animals have died.

hypotheses.rationale: Lamotrigine stabilizes neuronal membranes by modulating sodium channels, and reduced neural overexcitation can lower systemic stress and promote longevity in Caenorhabditis elegans.

hypotheses.title: Reserpine Shortens Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Reserpine shortens lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. Treatment with reserpine decreases mean and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Reserpine depletes monoamine stores and disrupts vesicular neurotransmission, which can impair feeding, movement, and stress regulation, thereby accelerating physiological decline in Caenorhabditis elegans.
hypotheses.prediction: Caenorhabditis elegans exposed to reserpine will show a statistically significant decrease in mean and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, treat one cohort with reserpine and a matched control with vehicle, and score survival daily under identical conditions until all animals die.

hypotheses.title: ABC101 Extends Lifespan via Insulin/IGF-1 Activation
hypotheses.claim: ABC101 extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by activating the insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway. The lifespan increase depends on activation of this pathway.
hypotheses.rationale: The insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway is a central regulator of aging in Caenorhabditis elegans, and its modulation governs stress resistance, metabolism, and longevity through conserved transcriptional programs.
hypotheses.prediction: ABC101-treated Caenorhabditis elegans will live longer than controls, and the extension will be abolished when core components of the insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway are removed or blocked.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare lifespan of ABC101-treated wild-type worms with ABC101-treated worms carrying loss-of-function mutations in key insulin/IGF-1 signaling components, and measure pathway target gene expression in both conditions.
